tldr: ERC-8004 is a Draft Ethereum standard that gives AI agents an ERC-721 identity pointing to a registration file, plus a public feedback registry. It moves no money. A validation registry is specified but not officially deployed.
whyItExists: An agent that wants to be hired by strangers needs a name others can look up, a list of where to reach it, and some record of how it behaved. Platform directories hold that data in one company's database. ERC-8004 puts the minimum on public chains instead: a transferable identity token, a pointer to a file that lists the agent's services, and a log where any client can leave a score with tags. Anyone can read it and build their own ranking on top, and payment stays with other protocols such as x402.

whatItIsNot.text: Not Final. ERC-8004 is a Draft: it moved to Review on 2025-10-08 and an EIP editor returned it to Draft on 2026-01-13, where it still is, even though registries are listed on 25 mainnets in the contracts README.
Not a payment protocol. The specification calls payments orthogonal and the registries have no payable function; x402 or any other rail moves the money.
Not three deployed registries. The Validation Registry is specified, but the contracts README lists no address for it on any chain.
Not a quality signal by itself. Agent counts are token ids, free to mint and full of placeholders; one study found only 3% to 15% of agents with a valid file and a live endpoint.
Not gated feedback any more. The agent-signed feedbackAuth was removed (contracts 2025-11-12, specification 2026-01-07); any address except the owner and operators can rate an agent.
Not know-your-agent or KYC. Registration is permissionless and nothing checks who runs an agent.
Not ERC-8183 or ERC-8126. ERC-8183 is job escrow with an evaluator and ERC-8126 is a separate verification standard; both build around ERC-8004.
Not the ERC-3643 Identity Registry. The T-REX registry maps wallets to issuer-attested identities for token transfers; the ERC-8004 one is an open ERC-721 agent directory.

changedRecently.text: ERC-8226 (Regulated Agent Mandate) was created as a Draft. It names ERC-8004 as the agent identity layer and adds a mandate layer for regulated tokens.
The Graph launched Agent0 subgraphs indexing ERC-8004 events on Base, BNB Chain, Ethereum, Monad and Polygon.
ERC-8126 (AI Agent Verification) reached Final, while ERC-8004, which it requires, stays Draft.
An empirical study (arXiv:2606.26028) found 3% to 15% of agents live and a majority of reviewers showing coordinated Sybil behavior, in data to 2026-05-13.
Robinhood Chain became the 25th mainnet in the contracts README, after 0G on 2026-06-11.
The CSOAI census read 505,635 agent ids on Ethereum, Base and BSC and found 13,210 that declare an http(s) MCP, A2A or web endpoint.
On-chain reads show one externally owned account owning all three registry proxies on Ethereum and Base; who holds it is not published.
